out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken stored,over raw lamb in the walk in cooler
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). PIC REARRANGED THE WALK IN

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: cooked meats and lentils in the walk in cooler
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC ADDED DATES TO FOOD.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: sun shine egg
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poisonous or Toxic Material
violations.observation: A container previously used to store poisonous or toxic materials is being used to store onions
violations.corrective_action: Do not store food in containers previously used to store poisonous or toxic materials. This practice may result in food contamination and subsequent medical consequences to anyone consuming the contaminated food. PIC DISCARDED ONIONS AND THE BUCKET.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: DOK Employee Health Policy
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide a verbal or written policy for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by an employee who has a disease or a medical condition. EHS observed no signed Employee Health policy.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge or certified food manager is responsible for knowledge, of at least the primary foodborne diseases (the Big 6) and medical conditions, to determine possible restriction or exclusion of food employees. EHS EMAILED FAIRFAX COUNTY EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY TO PIC. EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICIES NEED TO BE READ AND SIGNED BY ALL STAFF. PLEASE RETAIN THESE DOCUMENTS.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. EHS observed staff remove a dirty utensil lying in a container of ready to eat food with bare hands. EHS observed no hand washing from kitchen staff during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER HANDWASHING PROCEDURES. HANDS MUST BE WASHED WHEN CHANGING TASKS, RETURNING FROM THE BATHROOM, AND HANDLING RAW PRODUCTS.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a food preparation sink, warewashing sink or in a mop sink. All hand sinks were not properly stocked. PIC instructed EHS to wash in the mop sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EHS DID NOT WAS IN THE MOP SINK. EHS DISCUSSED THAT HAND WASHING IS DONE IN THE HAND SINK.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: EHS observed staff remove a dirty utensil from a container of ready-to-eat food. Bare hands came in contact with ready-to-eat food during the removal.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. EHS DISCUSSED WITH STAFF ABOUT HANDWASHING PROCEDURES AND WHEN TO WASH HANDS. EHS DISCUSSED WITH STAFF ABOUT USING GLOVES WHEN HANDLING READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: EHS observed no paper towels supplied at the hand sink in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. PIC PROVIDED PAPER TOWELS TO EHS.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: EHS observed no working hand soap at the hand sink in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. EHS WASHED HANDS AT THE HAND SINK AT THE SERVER STATION IN THE FRONT.

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: Both handwashing sinks in the kitchen and in the server area were blocked, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. EHS DISCUSSED THAT HAND WASHING SINKS CANNOT BE BLOCKED.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. EHS observed no hand washing sign at the hand sink in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS DISCUSSED WITH STAFF THAT A HANDWASHING SIGN MUST BE POSTED.

out_items.name: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

violations.title: Safe, Unadulterated & Honestly Presented
violations.observation: EHS observed a block of moldy cheese in the 2DR prep top cooler.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food shall be safe, unadulterated and honestly presented as specified under 3-601.12. PIC DISCARDED THE CHEESE.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: several storage containers of different RAW animal proteins were observed being stored over cooked ready-to-eat foods in the walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT THE PROPER STORAGE ORDER. RAW ANIMAL PROTEIN CANNOT BE STORED ABOVE READY-TO-EAT. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE REORGANIZE THE WALK-IN AND NOW ALL RAW FOOD IS PROPERLY STORED UNDER RTE FOODS.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean after Use
violations.observation: Equipment food-contact surfaces/utensils were not observed cleaned before any possible contamination. EHS observed a stand mixer encrusted with flour.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT MORE FREQUENT CLEANING MUST BE DONE.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: a container of minced garlic and herbs on a shelf along the prep line; blocks of butter, milk, and half and half in the 2DR glass display; large pot of chicken curry sauce on the floor under dirty dishes.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED ALL OF THE MENTIONED ITEMS. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT THE PROPER TEMPERATURE TO COLD HOLD FOOD. Spice Circle LLC (Inspection Date: 01/31/2025) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: EHS observed no date marking on cooked food in the walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS DISCUSSED WIITH PIC THAT FOOD THAT IS STORED FOR 24HR MUST BE DATE MARKED WITH WHEN IT WAS PREPARED AND WHEN IT IS TO BE DISCARDED. DISCARD ANY LEFTOVER FOOD AFTER 7 DAYS.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: a box of chicken thawing on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC PUT THE BOX OF CHICKEN BACK IN THE WALK IN COOLER. PROPER THAWING CAN BE DONE BY PLACING THE FROZEN ITEMS IN A COOLER OR UNDER RUNNING WATER.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. EHS observed the following food stored directly on the floor: large pot of chicken curry sauce; container of cooked chicken.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC DISCARDED THE MENTIONED ITEMS AWAY. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT FOOD CANNOT BE STORED DIRECTLY ON THE FLOOR. NSF APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACK SHOULD BE USED.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed that clean kitchen utensil being stored in an old milk jug.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean single-service and single-use articles in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor, unless kept in closed packages on pallets, racks, or skids. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT KITCHEN UTENSILS CANNOT BE STORED IN MILK CONTAINERS DUE TO CROSS CONTAMINATION ISSUES.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer spice containers were observed store different sauces in the 2DR prep top.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. PIC DISCARDED THE SAUCES. EHS DISCUSSED THAT CONTAINERS OF SPICE, GARLIC CONTAINERS, ETC. CANNOT BE REUSED.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not finished to have a smooth, cleanable surface: large mixer was observed with caked with flour; microwave was observed with food splatter on the interior.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be finished to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP THAT MORE CLEANING IS REQUIRED. Spice Circle LLC (Inspection Date: 01/31/2025) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: EHS observed a pH test kit and a quaternary ammonia test kit in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: PIC NEEDS TO PURCHASE A BLEACH/CHLORINE TEST KIT.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: floor surrounding the mixer; floor surrounding the cook line; exterior of kitchen equipment along the cook line; table next to the fryer; walls along the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS DISCUSSED MORE FREQUENT CLEANING IS REQUIRED.
